Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testNodeSetOperations` from `CoreOperationTest` checks the XPath expression `$array > 0` is evaluated to `Boolean.TRUE`. The failure relates to binary operator behavior on node-sets. According to the XPath spec quoted in the bug report, if both operands in a comparison are node-sets, the comparison should succeed if any node in the first set compared to any node in the second set yields true for the comparison on the string values of those nodes. Furthermore, if comparing a node-set to a number, the comparison is true if any node in the node-set compares true to the number. The failing test indicates the core binary operation implementation for such semantics is incorrect.

From the investigation attempts, no direct `evaluate` or helper method in `CoreOperation` matching typical names like `evaluateCompare` or `evaluateNodeSetOperands` was located, but likely the method to implement this behavior is inside the `CoreOperation` class or a class handling binary operations. The problem arises because the current implementation probably treats node-sets and numbers (or other node-sets) incorrectly, either by evaluating the whole node-set as one unit or not iterating over individual nodes as required by the XPath spec. The XPath spec requires an "existential" comparison semantics over the Cartesian product of nodes in both sets, which often is a subtle bug in XPath implementations.

Hence, the root cause is the implementation logic of the binary operator evaluation involving node-sets inside `CoreOperation` (or closely related computation classes) does not correctly implement the XPath specification for node-set comparisons, leading to incorrect boolean results in cases like `$array > 0`.

The best fix location will be the method responsible for evaluating binary operations involving node-sets in `CoreOperation` or a specific subclass dealing with core XPath operations.

Next step: locate the method in `CoreOperation` or a related class that implements binary operator evaluation on node-sets.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
